title: Layouts
subject: ui
summary: The page: shells and regions, their anatomy, the primitives that emit them, the container, the breakpoints, who owns the shell.

axioms.text: A page is a fixed tree of regions.
A region frames content and knows nothing of it.
The application owns the shell; a slice never builds one.
A region reacts to the viewport through the states it offers; which state at which width is the theme's.

purpose.intro: Every page of every product is the same tree of regions, so a reader knows where a thing is before reading the page, a theme can size and style every region once, and a slice page composes inside the regions without deciding the frame.

claims.text: **Columns** (`PageLeftSidebar`, `PageRightSidebar`, `MainRightSidebar`, `Main`) — width is set by the theme (`Main` takes what is left), height grows to the parent's max.
**Containers** (`PageBody`, `MainBody`) — flex rows that fill the remaining height after their header sibling. They carry their own structural defaults; you do not need to add sizing classes to them.
Scroll: `main-body` scrolls the page; inside a container the `Content` part scrolls (`overflow` per axis), see Markup rules. `ScrollArea` is to sunset; never add `overflow: auto/scroll` by hand.

reference.statement: Rows (`PageHeader`, `SecondPageHeader`, `MainHeader`, `SecondMainHeader`, `MainFooter`, `PageFooter`) — height is set by the theme, width grows to fill the parent.

claims.text: Overlays (Dialog, Sheet) are handled by the component library as `element="overlay--*"` surfaces, not layout regions. They are independent of the page tree.

reference.statement: Every structural region carries a `layout` attribute. A div is **either** `layout` or `element`, never both. The theme engine styles `layout` regions (background, border, etc.) the same way it styles `element` surfaces — the layout components never emit visual CSS themselves.

shell                          ← outermost viewport frame
├── shell-side-nav             ← global sidebar (fixed, collapsible)
├── shell-top-nav              ← global top bar (sticky)

page                           ← everything inside the shell content area

│   ├── page-left-sidebar      ← the page's left column (e.g. a section's nav)
│   ├── main                   ← primary column, fills remaining space
│   │   ├── main-header        ← full-width region spanning main (sticky optional)
│   │   ├── second-main-header ← optional second full-width row under main-header
│   │   ├── main-content       ← invisible row: main-body + main-right-sidebar

│   │   │   │   └── main-container ← width-constrained content wrapper (scale + align)
│   │   │   └── main-right-sidebar ← aside inside main (e.g. properties, knowledge)
│   │   └── main-footer        ← full-width region at the bottom of main
│   └── page-right-sidebar     ← the page's right column (e.g. activity feed)
└── page-footer                ← full-width row under everything, sidebars included

scroll-area                    ← canonical internal scroll container (use anywhere)

claims.text: **shell-side-nav**
**shell-none**
MINIMAL PAGE
**Mental model:**
**Cols** (ShellNav, PageLeftSidebar, PageRightSidebar, MainRightSidebar, MainBody): `width` set by theme, height fills parent (`align-self: stretch` or `flex: 1`)
**Rows** (Shell, Page, PageBody, Main, MainContent): `height` set by theme or fills parent (`flex: 1`), width is always `100%`
**Fixed edges** (PageHeader, SecondPageHeader, MainHeader, SecondMainHeader, MainFooter, PageFooter): `flex-shrink: 0` — they never shrink; the remaining space goes to MainContent
All structural flex defaults are **engine-hardcoded** — not theme-overridable. Theme controls surfaces, widths, and heights only.

The `page` region sits inside the shell content area. `page-body` is the flex row. `second-page-header` and `second-main-header` are optional: a second row under the page header (e.g. the tabs of the page) and under the main header. Use them in order, never alone: no second row without the first. `main-header` spans the full width of the `main` column — it is NOT inside `page-left-sidebar` or `page-right-sidebar`.
`page-right-sidebar` and `main-right-sidebar` can coexist — the flex layout handles both simultaneously (e.g. activity feed + properties panel).

reference.statement: `main-container` is the only layout region that accepts configuration props:

| Prop | Values | Default | Notes |
|------|--------|---------|-------|
| `scale` | `xs` `sm` `md` `lg` `xl` | `lg` | The reading measure. The theme gives each scale its max-width (`layouts.container` in the theme); the page never writes a number |
| `align` | `left` `center` `right` | `center` | Where the measure sits inside main-body |
| `position` | `fill` … | — | As on every region; `fill` = edge to edge, no measure |

reference.statement: A layout region breaks on the viewport. The primitive implements the states a region can take; the theme says at which viewport width a region takes which state and which width (`layouts.<region>`). The primitive decides nothing.

reference.topic: Ownership › The application owns the shell
reference.statement: Each route file picks a shell variant and wraps the page content. The route MUST use the layout primitives — `Shell`, `ShellSideNav`, `ShellTopNav`, `ShellNone`, `Page` — so the theme engine can target them.

reference.topic: Ownership › Layout components handle structural behavior only
reference.statement: Scroll, overflow, collapse, breakpoints, sticky positioning. They render `layout="..."` attributes. They know nothing about content or visual appearance. The theme engine handles visuals.

reference.topic: Ownership › Slices compose with the primitives and patterns
reference.statement: A slice page never builds its own shell. Inside the shell it composes with the layout primitives, following the layout patterns; a structure shared by a section's pages is a slice layout, composed once.

claims.text: **A layout zone primitive holds container zones.** A part zone (a header, a content, a stack) is never placed in a region on its own; it divides a container.
**`layout` or `element`, never both.** A div is the structural frame OR the morphological surface inside it. Never mix them.
**Layout components own all structural decisions.** Scroll, overflow, collapse, breakpoints, sticky. Page authors fill slots — they never write structural CSS.
**The theme engine styles layout regions.** `layout="page-left-sidebar"` gets background, border, width from the theme. The layout component itself emits no visual CSS.
**`main-header` spans the full `main` column.** It is not inside `page-left-sidebar`. It is a full-width region at the top of `main`, sitting above `main-body`.
**Slices never build their own shell or navigation.** The application owns the shell; a page composes the primitives inside it.

reference.statement: The package exports the primitives, and the layout patterns it ships.

A layout pattern is a composition of the primitives written once to be followed. The application layouts are named by their structure, never by their consumer; a slice layout (SettingsLayout, OrganizationLayout…) wears one of them. Outlets are named by the region they fill. Slots are typed as `React.ReactNode`.

imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| Export | Slots | Notes |
|--------|-------|-------|
| `DoubleSidebarLayout` | `pageHeaderContent`, `pageLeftSidebarContent`, `mainContainerContent`, `scale` | shell nav + page header + page left sidebar + main-container |
| `SingleSidebarLayout` | `pageHeaderContent`, `mainContainerContent`, `scale` | shell nav + page header + main-container |
| `BareLayout` | `mainContainerContent`, `scale` | shell nav + main-container |
| `AuthPage` | `children` | shell-none + a centred `main-container` at `scale="xs"` |

reference.statement: The zone primitives of the page: shell zone primitives (shell…) and layout zone primitives (page…, main…, the sidebars). Every page composes with them. Stack is not one: it is a part zone, exported from `@libs/web-components` (kept here as a re-export for one round).
